articles.author: talal qasim
articles.description:
When I started using TypeScript, the errors felt overwhelming.
👉 TypeScript errors are warnings, not obstacles.
Here are some common ones every developer sees:
❌ Property does not exist on type
This usually means your type definition doesn’t fully match your data.
❌ Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'
A classic example of TypeScript saving you from runtime bugs.
❌ Object is possibly 'undefined'
A reminder to handle edge cases before they reach production.
❌ Implicit 'any' type
Explicit types improve readability, maintainability, and team collaboration.
Why this matters
Each TypeScript error you fix:
Prevents bugs before runtime
Makes your code safer and more predictable
Improves long-term scalability
Type safety > runtime surprises 🚀
If you’re still writing plain JavaScript, TypeScript is one of the best upgrades you can make.
articles.title: TypeScript Errors Are Not Annoying They’re Helpful

articles.description:
TL;DR


Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) is a hidden AI security threat where malicious instructions reach a language model through trusted content like documents, APIs, or web pages. This can cause data leaks, unauthorized actions, and intellectual property theft without any visible signs. IPI is especially dangerous in automated workflows and enterprise systems. Effective defense requires layered measures including input validation, context segmentation, output filtering, human review, model fine-tuning, and continuous monitoring. Ignoring IPI is no longer an option because a single hidden instruction can turn your AI into a weapon.
The landscape of cybersecurity is in constant flux, but few developments have introduced a threat as fundamental and complex as the rise LLMs and autonomous A…
articles.title: Indirect Prompt Injection: The Complete Guide

articles.description:
In 2025, fintech adoption skyrocketed as apps rushed to add BTC features. This growth exposed a fatal flaw: most infrastructure models weren’t ready to handle that level of load.
A payment-app founder I know learned this the hard way, when a successful reward campaign triggered a sharp 10x surge in active users. It was a big W for the marketing team, but a disaster for devs - because their backend layer started to collapse.
At that critical moment, they stood at a crossroads with 2 paths:
🔴 Path 1: The "Patch & Pray" Approach. They could try to salvage their legacy system, sentencing the dev team to endless maintenance cycles and sleepless nights fixing critical bugs, which would slow down the roadmap to patch a dam that was already bursting.
🟢 Path 2: The Infrastructure Pivot. They could re-architect the backend using WhiteBIT’s Wallet-as-a-Service. This path offered more than just a fix - it promised instant app stability, lightning-fast deposits and withdrawals, turning their infrastructure into a limitless engine for growth.
The choice was obvious. By integrating WaaS, they seamlessly upgraded their platform, optimized performance, and gave the dev team their weekends back.

Leadership in today’s world requires more than managing tasks or holding a position of authority. It calls for emotional steadiness, clear thinking, and the ability to elevate others while continually improving oneself. The philosophy influenced by Joshua Moll places personal development at the core of effective leadership, blending practical coaching tools with the internal discipline needed to thrive in complexity. His approach emphasizes that the journey toward influence begins within—through awareness, resilience, and intentional action—and expands outward through communication, coaching, and relationship-building.
This article explores how this framework strengthens leaders, helps them navigate adversity, and builds the foundation for long-term self-mastery.

From Solver to Facilitator: Leaders empower others by guiding them instead of providing every solution.
Joshua Moll, emphasizing growth over perfection.
Schedule consistent coaching conversations
Leadership is not static—it is a lifelong practice shaped by mindset, discipline, and relationship. The teachings inspired by Joshua Moll remind leaders that growth starts within and expands outward through communication, coaching, and resilience. When leaders cultivate self-mastery, embrace adversity, and empower others with intention, they create a ripple effect that strengthens teams and transforms organizational culture. The storms of leadership are inevitable, but a leader grounded in clarity and purpose always steers the ship with confidence.
